correctness.rationale: TARGET route: verified both bounds from first principles. Upper: Weil (deg-4, m<=4 gives |S|<=3sqrt(p)+1 for m2!=0; S(m1,0)=-1) into standard 2D Erdos-Turan-Koksma with H=floor(sqrt(p)) yields C p^{-1/2}(log p)^2; phase identity e(m2{h^4/p})=e_p(m2 h^4) is exact. Lower: G_p dominates second-marginal 1D discrepancy at a=1; Koksma gives G_p>=|T|/(2pi N); character identity n_a=sum chi^j(a) gives T_1=g(chi)+g(phi)+g(chibar); p=5 mod24 gives p=1 mod4 so g(phi)=sqrt(p) and p=5 mod8 so chi(-1)=-1 hence g(chi)+g(chibar) purely imaginary, Re(T_1)=sqrt(p), |T|>=sqrt(p)/2, G_p>=c p^{-1/2} with c=1/(8pi); Dirichlet gives infinitely many such primes, all 5 mod12. Independently re-ran verify_gauss.py: all 12 primes agree to <1e-13.

originality.rationale: Headline is the exact two-sided rate for P_p={(h/p,{h^4/p})}, p=5 mod12, with log-free lower bound on 5 mod24. scope_literature_search was attempted three times but timed out after internal retries (partial-coverage failure recorded); continued with direct Crossref/OpenAlex/arXiv queries. No prior source states this point-set discrepancy rate. Nearest priors are generic tools (Weil+ETK, Koksma, quadratic/quartic Gauss evaluations, Niederreiter low-discrepancy constructions, quartic-sum power-mean papers) which supply lemmas but do not imply or tabulate the combined residue-specific headline. Adversarial checks for synonyms, encodings, broader theorems, and databases found no covering result.

value.rationale: TARGET resolution proving both sides of an admitted uniform-distribution/finite-field equidistribution target: matching Theta(p^{-1/2}) rate up to logs for a natural monomial curve, with an exact Gauss-period identity Re(sum e_p(x^4))=sqrt(p) as the mechanism. Object and invariant were motivated before computation, value is not known or mechanically implied, and future work on polynomial-curve discrepancy needs the precise rate. Not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration; constants are unoptimized but the rate is the substance.
